digest.component_or_area: enrichment queue and digest history reduction
propositions: Physical deletion of committed queue and digest events causes git rename-detection conflicts on cross-clone merge because identical deletions are paired with distinct UUID-based additions.
Current queue reduction reads every matching file per event type (4,977 opens per full-store scan), causing the enrichment drain gate to breach its 20ms budget at 400-544ms observed latency.

The event filename format ({timestamp}-{uuid}-{TYPE}.json) has lexicographically-ordered timestamps identical to event body timestamps, enabling a newest-first suffix read that reduces file opens to 1,658 without deletion.
Deleting committed files reclaims zero repository space because blobs remain in git history; physical prune eliminates checkout bytes only while adding 2,473 merge commits and breaking reconvergence.
A merge-safe removal must rename to a deterministic source-derived path with identical content; any deletion paired with a fresh-UUID add violates this rule and re-wedges the merge.

The designed read-bound (≤3+k opens per ticket for reduce_ticket, ≤c opens for claim arbitration, 1 open for latest_ticket_digest) preserves all events, requires no deletion or compaction, and remains valid under cross-clone union merge.
